xmldoc.short_description: Read a recording in the EDF or EDF+ format.

param_input_item.param_description: the path to the EDF or EDF+ file.
the leads to return, by label (a char or a cellstr) or by index into the non annotation signals; by default every signal whose label names an ECG lead, and every signal when none does.
whether to read the 'EDF Annotations' signal into the recording's annotations (true by default).

param_output_item.param_description: the module's recording struct, the same one every other reader returns, so nothing downstream can tell an EDF file from a WFDB record.

description.p: The EDF, EDF+, BDF and BDF+ binary format is read by the edf toolbox, a dependency of this module, so the header arithmetic and the little-endian (or BDF 24-bit) samples are handled in one place; this reader only maps the neutral struct it returns onto the ecglab recording. A stored integer becomes a physical value by physical = (digital - dmin) * (pmax - pmin) / (dmax - dmin) + pmin, and reading that arithmetic wrongly gives a signal that looks entirely plausible and is wrong.

Signals may be sampled at different rates. The selected leads are returned at the highest rate among them, the slower ones held sample by sample within each data record, and recording.info.rates keeps the native rate of each so a slow channel is not mistaken for a fast one resampled.

The 'EDF Annotations' signal is never returned as a lead; it is a byte stream, not a physiological channel. It carries time-stamped annotation lists (TALs): an onset with a sign, an optional duration after the byte 21, one or more texts separated by the byte 20, and the list ended by a zero. Each text becomes an annotation at sample round(onset * rate) + 1; a single PhysioNet symbol becomes the symbol, any other text becomes the note symbol with the text kept in aux, and a duration is kept in num, in samples. The first TAL of each record is a time stamp with an empty text and carries no annotation.

The patient field X X X X is the format's anonymous patient and becomes the subject anonymous. The start date and time go to recording.info.startDate (DD/MM/YYYY) and recording.info.startTime (HH.MM.SS) with startTimeKnown true; the two digit year is expanded with the format's rule, 85 to 99 being the 1900s and 00 to 84 the 2000s.

An EDF+D (discontinuous) file is read as if continuous, with recording.info.discontinuous true and a note in the comments, because the rest of the module works on one uniform timeline; the per-record gaps of such a file are not reconstructed.

xmldoc.bibliography: Kemp and Olivan, European data format 'plus' (EDF+), Clinical Neurophysiology 114(9), 2003; Kemp et al., A simple format for exchange of digitized polygraphic recordings, Electroencephalography and Clinical Neurophysiology 82(5), 1992.
